blocks.x: Cyber & Zero-Trust for Payments & Cards: what the sector's controls demand, what we build on the platform rails, and the outcomes written into the engagement.

Payments is a real-time decision business: instant rails compress fraud windows to seconds, authorization economics reward millisecond latency, and every innovation (click-to-pay, tokenized wallets) inherits the same decision spine.

items: Continuous-compliance expectations replace annual snapshots; tokenization and segmentation evidence is assembled manually.
Fraud and risk enrichment adds milliseconds that cost approval rates; batch components cannot sit on the instant path.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Cyber Resilience & Incident Recovery, Compliance, Audit & Digital Trust, Cloud Security & Posture Management from the Cybersecurity & Zero-Trust tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Authorization decisioning, Chargeback/dispute handling, Scheme settlement reconciliation) on Dataq Sentinel and Dataq Compass. Governance inherits the sector frame — PCI DSS 4.0 among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Identity as the perimeter: workforce, customer and machine identities on one governed plane.
Secure at the control plane: posture, workload and data security engineered into the platform.
Secure the models themselves: prompt-injection defense, agent containment and AI red-teaming.
Tokenization, segmentation and continuous evidence (audit prep automated)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Banking & Financial Services level this capability reads as: third-party register, incident playbooks and control tests continuously evidenced (assessment preparation down from quarters to weeks). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Every program of this type runs the same weekly rhythm, so your team can plan around it. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline with your team: the current metric is measured, signed and stored as the reference for every later gate. Weeks 3–8 run the pilot on deliberately narrow scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, never quietly extended.
